```{r, echo = FALSE}
library(EMC2)
```

## Loading a network is not the same as being able to infer with it

*EMC2* ships two normalizing flows: **DDMnle** (a single flow for the full DDM,
covering all combinations of variability parameters) and a flow for the **racing
diffusion model**. Both are loaded with `register_nn_model()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
DDMnle <- register_nn_model(
  system.file("extdata/flownn/ddm_sc_s1106_e245_weights.json", package = "EMC2"),
  twin = DDM)

RDMnle <- register_nn_model(
  system.file("extdata/flownn/rdm_ss_base_s801_e271_weights.json", package = "EMC2"),
  twin = RDM)
```

A registered model is used exactly like `DDM` or `RDM`: it goes into `design()`,
gets a prior, is fitted. Any network registered with `register_nn_model()` —
including likelihood approximation networks converted from ONNX — follows the
same pattern.

A network is an approximation, trained on simulations from part of the
parameter space. Its error is not a constant: where it varies with the
parameters it moves the posterior, and a model that looks accurate point by
point can still be biased where it matters for inference. So a network has to
be checked, against the exact likelihood, before its posteriors are believed.
This vignette describes the checks *EMC2* provides and what they found for the
shipped networks. The reasoning behind them, and the mistakes they guard
against, are documented in the NLE project's handover notes (Wuth, 2026:
`METHODS.md` section 6, "What the diagnostics can and cannot do", and
`TRAPS.md`); they are not restated here.

## A single DDM flow for all variability cases

DDMnle was trained with a zero-box regime: the training data includes exact
zeros for `sv`, `SZ` and `st0` as a separate sampling regime. A single network
therefore covers the analytic DDM (all three set to zero) and every subcase in
between. Subcases are selected in `design()` via `constants`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
DDMnle <- register_nn_model(
  system.file("extdata/flownn/ddm_sc_s1106_e245_weights.json", package = "EMC2"),
  twin = DDM)

# sv = 0, st0 = 0 (only SZ free):
des_SZonly <- design(factors = list(subjects = 1), Rlevels = c("u", "l"),
                     model = DDMnle,
                     formula = list(v ~ 1, a ~ 1, t0 ~ 1, Z ~ 1, SZ ~ 1),
                     constants = c(sv = -Inf, st0 = -Inf))  # -Inf on log scale = 0

# analytic DDM (all variability fixed to zero):
des_ddm <- design(factors = list(subjects = 1), Rlevels = c("u", "l"),
                  model = DDMnle,
                  formula = list(v ~ 1, a ~ 1, t0 ~ 1, Z ~ 1),
                  constants = c(sv = -Inf, SZ = -Inf, st0 = -Inf))
```

The old DDMnn cards (`ddm_cap256w_c4`, `ddm_st0zero`) required a different
network for each subcase because they were not trained with zero-box sampling;
DDMnle replaces them all. They remain in the package for backward compatibility.

## A cell: the network and its control, differing in one respect

Every check runs on a *cell*: one design with independent normal priors on
the sampled scale, built twice, once with the network and once with an
analytic *control*, by default the model the network approximates (for
`DDMnle`, `DDM`). The two cells share the design, constants, defaults, prior
and simulator; they differ in the likelihood only. The same check on the
control must come out at about zero; what it does show is not the network's
doing.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
DDMnle <- register_nn_model(
  system.file("extdata/flownn/ddm_sc_s1106_e245_weights.json", package = "EMC2"),
  twin = DDM)

cell <- nn_cell(DDMnle,
  mean = c(v = 1, a = log(.8), t0 = log(.3), Z = qnorm(.5), SZ = qnorm(.2),
           sv = log(.1), st0 = log(.05)),
  sd = c(v = .15, a = .15, t0 = .1, Z = .05, SZ = .15, sv = .15, st0 = .15))
cell
```

Priors are always named (never matched by position). Parameters not given a
prior stay at the model's default, which must lie inside the network's
training region. The within-trial noise `s` is held at its default by default,
as it sets the scale.

**The prior must stay inside the training region.** The network rejects
parameter vectors outside the region it was trained on, which truncates the
posterior there. For an SBC that is fatal: a replicate whose true parameters
lie outside cannot be recovered. `nn_cell()` refuses a prior whose mean +- 4 sd
leaves the region, and `run_sbc()` makes the same check (`nn_in_box()`) for
every neural-likelihood design:

```{r, error = TRUE}
RDMnle <- register_nn_model(
  system.file("extdata/flownn/rdm_ss_base_s801_e271_weights.json", package = "EMC2"),
  twin = RDM)
des <- design(factors = list(subjects = 1), Rlevels = c("a", "b"), model = RDMnle,
              formula = list(v ~ 0 + lR, B ~ 1, t0 ~ 1, A ~ 1), constants = c(s = log(1)),
              report_p_vector = FALSE)
pri <- prior(des, type = "single",
             pmean = c(v_lRa = log(2), v_lRb = log(1), B = 0, t0 = log(.2), A = log(.3)),
             psd = c(v_lRa = .1, v_lRb = .1, B = .1, t0 = .5, A = .1))
nn_in_box(des, pri)
```

## Four checks, cheapest first

```{r, eval = FALSE}
nn_total_mass(cell)                                   # seconds
nn_score_bias(cell, n_draws = 200)                    # seconds
nn_posterior_shift(cell, n_datasets = 60, cores = 8)  # about a minute
nn_sbc_cell(cell, trials = 400, replicates = 500,     # hours
            cores_per_chain = 8, cores_for_chains = 1,
            archive_dir = "2026-10-01_dev-flow_ddmnle-sbc")
```

**Total mass** (`nn_total_mass()`) integrates the network's likelihood over rt
and responses for parameter vectors drawn from the prior. A flow integrates to
one by construction; a network that regresses the log-likelihood does not,
which is harmless while the log mass is constant in the parameters (it cancels
from the posterior). The same integral of the control on the same grid
separates the network from the grid. The column `before_support` is the mass
the network puts before the non-decision time, where the exact density is
zero. A flow's support is all rt > 0, so it smears the leading edge of the
distribution a little, the region that informs the non-decision time.

**Score bias** (`nn_score_bias()`) is the expected score of the network's
log-likelihood at the true parameters, per trial: zero for an exact
likelihood, and the direction in which the network pulls the posterior
otherwise. It is computed by quadrature over rt (weighted by the control's
likelihood) and a central difference, so the control's own score bias must be
about zero; if it is not, the estimator is at fault, not the network.
Parameters that move the support (`t0`) are excluded. Score bias is local: it
ranks networks of one architecture but does not predict SBC bias across
architectures. It is necessary, not sufficient.

**Posterior shift** (`nn_posterior_shift()`) computes what an SBC cell
computes, without the sampler: for data sets simulated from the prior, the
posterior under the network and under the control (Laplace approximations
refined by importance sampling), and from them the standardised bias of each
posterior mean, `mean(post mean - truth) / sd(post mean - truth)`, the shift
of the network's posterior from the control's in posterior sds, and the ratio
of posterior sds. The control column must be within Monte Carlo error of zero
(standard error about `1 / sqrt(n)`); the paired shift is much more precise
than either column. In the NLE project it predicted the standardised bias of
500-replicate SBC cells within about 0.1. Use it to screen, not to certify.

**An SBC cell with its control** (`nn_sbc_cell()`) is the confirmation: it
runs `run_sbc()` on the network's cell and on the control's, summarises both
(`nn_sbc_summary()`: standardised bias, with the gate |value| <= 0.5; coverage;
the KS test of the ranks; the ECDF envelope), and, given `archive_dir`, writes
the run in the layout of the EMC2 SBC archive. With `run = FALSE` it only
writes the bundle (the cell and a script that runs it), to be copied to a
cluster. In `run_sbc()`, `cores_per_chain` is the number of replicates fitted
at once, and each fit runs its chains in parallel too (`cores_for_chains`,
by default the number of chains), so the call above with
`cores_for_chains = 1` uses 8 cores, and without it 24.

None of these checks identifiability: SBC passes by construction for a
parameter the data do not inform. For a new model, add parameter recovery
with the prior centred away from the truth, and likelihood profiles.

## What the checks found for the shipped networks

All numbers are on the sampled scale (log for `a`, `t0`, `sv`, `st0`, `B`,
`A`, the rates of the race; probit for `Z`, `SZ`; `v` is sampled directly).
The script `system.file("scripts", "nle_validation_kit.R", package = "EMC2")`
reproduces the numbers.

### DDMnle (sc_s1106_e245)

DDMnle was validated on six variability cases (N = 400, 500 replicates each,
AWS x86_64): `sv = 0`, `SZ = 0`, `st0 = 0`, `sv = SZ = 0`, `sv = st0 = 0`,
and the full model (all free). The prior was the cell above. Score bias was
screened before SBC on all six cases (300 prior draws, H = 0.01, oracle
control g <= 7e-5; `t0` excluded because it moves the support).

**Total mass** (50 prior draws): mean `log Z` < 2e-5, sd < 1.1e-5, mass
before support < 2e-5 in every case — consistent with a normalised flow.

**Score bias** (300 draws, standard error in brackets):

| case | v | a | Z | sv | SZ | st0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | +0.0001 (0.0000) | +0.0015 (0.0002) | -0.0024 (0.0001) | 0.0000 (0.0000) | -0.0003 (0.0000) | +0.0007 (0.0000) |
| sv = 0 | +0.0002 (0.0000) | -0.0032 (0.0002) | -0.0002 (0.0000) | — | +0.0001 (0.0000) | -0.0007 (0.0000) |
| SZ = 0 | -0.0002 (0.0000) | +0.0037 (0.0001) | +0.0014 (0.0000) | 0.0000 (0.0000) | — | +0.0004 (0.0000) |
| st0 = 0 | +0.0001 (0.0001) | +0.0030 (0.0008) | -0.0023 (0.0003) | 0.0000 (0.0000) | -0.0003 (0.0000) | — |
| sv = SZ = 0 | -0.0002 (0.0000) | +0.0040 (0.0001) | -0.0049 (0.0001) | — | — | -0.0001 (0.0000) |
| sv = st0 = 0 | +0.0002 (0.0001) | -0.0023 (0.0010) | -0.0013 (0.0003) | — | +0.0001 (0.0000) | — |
| sv = SZ = st0 = 0 | -0.0003 (0.0000) | +0.0047 (0.0007) | -0.0061 (0.0003) | — | — | — |

Score biases are 5–20x smaller than the old DDMnn cards (`a` 0.0030–0.0047
here vs 0.0153 for ddm_cap256w_c4 and 0.0338 for ddm_st0zero).

**SBC** (N = 400, 500 replicates; gate |standardised bias| <= 0.5):
all 35 parameter-case tests pass the gate. Worst |std bias|: 0.13 (t0,
full case). Coverage: 0.922–0.972. Minimum KS p: 0.020. One case
(full) had one parameter outside the ECDF envelope — chance level for
35 tests. The old DDMnn cards had worst |std bias| 0.15–0.50.

**Speed** vs WienR (N = 400, single thread, compiled path):

| case | WienR (ms) | DDMnle (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| full | 1.19 | 0.13 | ~9x |
| sv = 0 | 1.17 | 0.13 | ~9x |
| st0 = 0 | 1.21 | 0.12 | ~10x |
| SZ = 0 | 0.35 | 0.08 | ~4x |

### RDM flow (rdm_ss_base_s801_e271)

The RDM flow was validated on a two-accumulator cell (v ~ lM, prior means
`v = log(1.5)`, `v_lMTRUE = 0.4`, `B = 0`, `A = log(0.3)`, `t0 = log(0.2)`,
sds 0.1) and on an A = 0 cell (the boundary-onset case).

**Total mass** (50 prior draws): mean `log Z` < 2e-5, sd < 1.1e-5, mass
before support < 2e-5 — consistent with a normalised flow.

**SBC** (N = 400; gate |standardised bias| <= 0.5):

| cell | parameter | std bias | coverage | KS p | in gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard (500 rep.) | v | +0.038 | 0.940 | 0.693 | yes |
| | v_lMTRUE | -0.097 | 0.928 | 0.052 | yes |
| | B | +0.007 | 0.956 | 0.737 | yes |
| | A | -0.063 | 0.960 | 0.539 | yes |
| | t0 | +0.031 | 0.934 | 0.830 | no (ECDF only) |
| A = 0 (250 rep.) | v | +0.046 | 0.924 | 0.785 | yes |
| | v_lMTRUE | -0.017 | 0.956 | 0.901 | yes |
| | B | -0.006 | 0.940 | 0.911 | yes |
| | t0 | +0.056 | 0.948 | 0.893 | yes |

Both cells pass the gate. The `t0` ECDF exceedance in the standard cell
is marginal and shared by the analytic control (std bias -0.029), indicating
it comes from the prior's true parameter vectors rather than the network.

### LAN (ddm_uniform_st)

The LAN `ddm_uniform_st` (HSSM's DDM with uniform non-decision-time
variability, converted from ONNX) is an example of a third-party network.
From the score bias check (80 prior draws, rt grid to 60 s):

| network | parameter | g (se) |
|---|---|---|
| LAN `ddm_uniform_st` | v | +0.0000 (0.0024) |
| | a | -0.1098 (0.0037) |
| | z | -0.0094 (0.0027) |

The grid has to reach 60 s: with the default 8 s the control's g on `a`
is -0.005 because the region includes slow parameter vectors with
probability beyond 8 s. The LAN underestimates boundary separation by about
0.11 on the sampled scale (~0.8 posterior sds at 400 trials per the
posterior shift check) and should not be used for inference in this region
without further validation.

## Practical notes

- The checks and `run_sbc()` run their work in forked processes (`cores`,
  `cores_per_chain`). On macOS, *EMC2* keeps Apple's Accelerate library (the
  BLAS its compiled code uses there) single-threaded by setting
  `VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1` when it is loaded, because its multithreaded
  matrix products crash forked processes. On Linux with OpenBLAS, set
  `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` for the same reason (and to avoid
  oversubscription).
- A network registered from a file path must be at the same path wherever
  the cell is run; the shipped networks are accessed via `system.file()` as
  shown above.
- The CRDM (circular racing diffusion model) flow ships alongside the RDM
  flow; its card is in the same directory. Its validation is documented in
  the NLE project's handover notes.
